resolution: Diagnosed why the 5x2 face region refused to merge one-shot while staged sub-merges reached the same single face: mergeFaceIds cancelled seam edges by vertex id alone, so a T-junction seam (one face spanning in one edge run what the facing side splits at a mid-run vertex — cuts landing at different heights per column) left both sides looking like boundary and the walk refused. Fixed in framework/gpu/indexed_edit_mesh.zig by splitting every selected edge at selection vertices strictly inside it before cancellation — overlapping seam runs now decompose into sub-edges that cancel exactly, so the region merges in one shot. Holed/pinched selections still refuse. TS twin editMesh.ts got the identical rule. New repro tests both sides (152/152 zig test-mesh-edit green, TS suite green; the one TS FAIL is the pre-existing cylinder cap test, fails on baseline too). Docs + index record updated. NOTE: editor binary needs a rebuild to pick up the zig fix; heavy parity suites (mesh-port-parity ships the editor) deferred to a quiet moment per live-session rule.
